name: Chinese Home Cooking
summary: A week at the Chinese home table: congee and egg pancakes for breakfast, mapo tofu, red-braised beef, steamed fish and homemade dumplings for dinner, with mixed brown rice, whole-wheat noodles and plenty of greens.
howItWorks:
**Cook once, eat twice.** Monday's mapo tofu, Wednesday's chicken stir-fry, Friday's red-braised beef and Saturday's dumplings each make two portions, so Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday lunches are done. The millet porridge also feeds two breakfasts.

**Rice twice.** On Sunday, simmer 2 cups of brown rice with 1 cup of pearled barley and 6 cups of water for 45 minutes, then rest it for 10. On Thursday, cook half that. Extra freezes well. Roast the snack sweet potatoes on Sunday, too.

**Fish three times.** Scallion oil salmon on Tuesday and doubanjiang mackerel on Thursday carry the **omega-3 and vitamin D**, never on back-to-back days. Steamed sea bass on Sunday adds lean protein. Walnuts blended into soy milk, on the millet porridge and with pear help the balance, too.

**Tofu, greens and soy milk.** Calcium-set tofu, soy milk, gai lan, bok choy and napa do the calcium work without dairy. Eggs, shrimp and iodized salt help with iodine, and almonds and peanuts cover vitamin E.

**Salt with care.** Soy sauce, oyster sauce and doubanjiang are strong, so each recipe measures them, and black vinegar, ginger, scallion and Sichuan pepper's numbing tingle add the punch instead. Saturday is the long day, with the dumplings, and Friday's beef is hands-off but long.

recipes.name: Brown rice and barley congee with shrimp, bok choy and crushed peanuts
recipes.inspiredBy: Cantonese shrimp congee (har juk), made quickly from cooked grains and topped with crushed peanuts as in peanut congee
recipes.about: A soft and creamy rice porridge with sweet shrimp, ginger and bok choy, topped with crushed roasted peanuts, scallion and a few drops of sesame oil. It is built from the rice and barley you cooked on Sunday: simmer the base the night before, and in the morning it takes 5 minutes. The **shrimp carry the protein** and the peanuts add vitamin E and crunch.

ingredients.note: peeled and deveined, cut into pieces
about a 2 cm piece, thinly sliced

steps: The night before, while dinner cooks, put the rice and barley in a small pot with the sliced ginger and about 3 parts water to 1 part cooked grain by volume. Bring to a boil, then turn the heat down to a steady simmer.

Simmer for about 20 minutes, stirring now and then and pressing some of the grains against the side of the pot, until the grains have broken down and the congee is soft and creamy. Cool it and keep it in the fridge.
In the morning, reheat the base with a splash of water until it bubbles. Crush the peanuts roughly with the flat of a knife. Slice the scallion.
Toss the shrimp with the soy sauce and a pinch of white pepper and stir them into the congee. Cook for 2 minutes, until pink and curled.
Stir in the bok choy and the salt and cook for 1 minute, just until the leaves are bright green.
Ladle into a bowl and top with the scallion, the peanuts and a few drops of sesame oil.
recipes.tip: Congee is the great leftover rescuer. Any cooked rice and a handful of greens will do, and a spoon of rinsed zha cai on top is very Cantonese.

recipes.name: Whole-wheat scallion egg pancake with cucumber and warm soy milk
recipes.inspiredBy: Chinese street-cart egg pancakes (jianbing), made with whole-wheat flour and sweet bean sauce
recipes.about: A thin, chewy whole-wheat crepe with scallion in the batter, two eggs spread over the top and a smear of sweet bean sauce, rolled up around crunchy cucumber. A glass of warm soy milk goes alongside, the way it is sold at breakfast stands. The **whole wheat and eggs keep you full**, and the soy milk adds calcium.
steps: Whisk the flour with about twice as much water as flour by weight and the salt, until you have a thin, pourable batter like cream. Stir in half the scallion, finely sliced, and let it rest for 5 minutes while you get everything else ready.
Cut the cucumber into thin matchsticks. Stir the sweet bean sauce with a spoonful of water to loosen it into a spreadable sauce.

Warm a non-stick pan over medium heat and brush it with a little of the oil. Pour in the batter and tilt the pan to spread it as thin as a crepe. Cook for about 2 minutes, until the top looks dry and the edges lift. Flip it over.

Crack the eggs onto the pancake, break the yolks with your spatula and spread the egg out in a thin layer. Scatter on the rest of the scallion and the sesame seeds, and cook for another minute, until the egg is just set.
Spread the sweet bean sauce over the egg, lay the cucumber along one side and roll the pancake up tightly. Cut it in half.
Warm the soy milk in a small pot or in the microwave and serve it alongside.
recipes.tip: Add a few drops of chili oil under the cucumber if you like jianbing hot.

recipes.name: Millet and sweet potato porridge with a soy-simmered egg and tofu
recipes.inspiredBy: Northern Chinese xiaomi zhou, the millet porridge eaten with an egg and a crisp pickle on the side
recipes.about: A golden, creamy millet porridge cooked with chunks of sweet potato, topped with toasted walnuts and served with a firm soy-simmered egg, tofu and a tangy quick pickle of daikon. It is a slow weekend breakfast that makes two bowls, so Sunday morning is just a reheat. The millet and sweet potato bring **fibre and vitamin A**.

ingredients.note: calcium-set, check the label for calcium sulphate, cubed

steps: Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 10 minutes, until the whites and yolks are both firm. Cool them under cold water and peel.

In a small pot, bring the soy sauce, about 150 ml (⅔ cup) of water and the ginger to a gentle simmer. Add the tofu and simmer for 10 minutes. Slip the peeled eggs into the warm liquid and leave them there while the porridge cooks.
While the eggs and tofu sit, rinse the millet in a sieve until the water runs clear. Put it in a pot with the sweet potato and about 8 times as much water as millet by volume. Bring to a boil.
Turn the heat to low and simmer, partly covered, for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the millet is soft and the porridge is thick and creamy. The sweet potato will mostly melt into it.
Toss the daikon sticks with the black vinegar and a few drops of sesame oil, and let them sit while the porridge cooks. They should be crisp and tangy. Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes.
Serve a portion of porridge with a halved egg, some of the tofu and a spoonful of the soy liquid, the pickle on the side and the walnuts on top.
Keep the second portion of porridge in the fridge. It thickens overnight, so loosen it with a splash of water when you reheat it. The eggs and tofu keep well in their liquid.
recipes.tip: A strip of mandarin peel in the tofu's liquid is lovely.

recipes.name: Tomato and egg stir-fry over brown rice and barley
recipes.inspiredBy: Chinese tomato and egg stir-fry (fanqie chao dan)
recipes.about: The most-loved home dish in China: three tender egg curds, cooked through, folded into a jammy, sweet-sharp tomato sauce, spooned over rice. It is ready in about 20 minutes and is wonderful hot or at room temperature. The **tomatoes bring vitamin C and potassium**, and the eggs make it a proper lunch.
steps: Cut the tomatoes into wedges, slice the scallion whites and greens separately and mince the garlic. Beat the eggs with the salt and a few drops of sesame oil. Reheat the rice and barley.

Heat half the oil in a wok or wide pan over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Pour in the eggs and let them puff for about 15 seconds, then push them gently from the edges into the middle in big curds. Keep going for about 1 minute, until no runny egg is left, then take them out.
Add the rest of the oil to the same pan, then stir-fry the garlic and scallion whites for 10 seconds. Add the tomatoes, the soy sauce and the sugar, which balances the acid.
Cook, pressing the tomatoes now and then, for 3 to 4 minutes, until they collapse into a thick, jammy sauce. Splash in a little water if it gets dry.
Fold the eggs back in for 1 minute, so the curds soak up the sauce. Scatter with the scallion greens and serve over the rice and barley.
recipes.tip: Very ripe, sweet tomatoes? Cut the sugar to a pinch. Pale winter ones need all of it.

recipes.name: Egg fried brown rice with tofu, edamame and scallion
recipes.inspiredBy: Chinese egg fried rice, packed with tofu and edamame
recipes.about: Fried rice only works with cold, day-old rice, which is exactly what your batch in the fridge is. Fluffy egg, golden tofu and bright edamame are tossed over high heat until the grains jump and smell toasty. The **tofu and edamame add plant protein** and the tofu brings calcium.

ingredients.note: calcium-set, check the label for calcium sulphate, cut into small cubes

steps: Break up the cold rice and barley with wet hands so there are no clumps. Pat the tofu dry and cut it into small cubes. Mince the ginger and garlic, slice the scallion whites and greens separately, and beat the eggs.

Heat a wok or your widest pan over high heat until a drop of water sizzles at once. Add half the oil, then the tofu, and fry for 3 minutes, turning now and then, until golden on a few sides. Slide it onto a plate.
Add the rest of the oil, pour in the eggs and scramble them in a few seconds, breaking it into small pieces.

Add the ginger, garlic and scallion whites and stir-fry for 30 seconds. Tip in the rice and barley, press it flat against the pan for a few seconds, then toss. Keep going for 3 minutes, until the grains separate and you hear them popping.

Return the tofu, add the edamame, and drizzle the soy sauce and broth around the edge of the pan so they sizzle. Toss for another minute, then finish with the scallion greens and a pinch of white pepper.
recipes.tip: The pan has to be hot and the rice has to be cold. If you cook for two, fry in two batches so the rice fries instead of steams.

recipes.name: Whole-wheat noodles with beef and mushroom sauce, cucumber, carrot and daikon
recipes.inspiredBy: Beijing zhajiangmian, with whole-wheat noodles, extra mushrooms and tofu in the sauce
recipes.about: Chewy noodles under a dark, glossy sauce of lean minced beef, shiitake and tofu simmered with sweet bean paste, topped with a pile of raw cucumber, carrot and daikon matchsticks. Hot, savoury sauce meets cold, crunchy vegetables in every bite, which is the whole point of the dish. The **raw vegetable strips and whole-wheat noodles add fibre**.

ingredients.note: whole-wheat spaghetti stands in for whole-wheat noodles
calcium-set, check the label for calcium sulphate, crumbled

steps: Cut the cucumber, carrot and daikon into thin matchsticks and keep them in separate piles. Finely dice the shiitake, mince the ginger and garlic, and slice the scallion whites and greens separately.

Warm the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the beef and cook, breaking it up, for about 4 minutes, until it is no longer pink and starting to brown (71 °C / 160 °F inside). Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw beef. Add the ginger, garlic and scallion whites and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the shiitake and the crumbled tofu and cook for about 3 minutes, until the mushrooms soften and give up their liquid.

Push everything to one side and fry the sweet bean sauce in the oil that collects, stirring, for 1 to 2 minutes, until it smells deep and toasty and the oil separates. Stir it through the beef, add the soy sauce and pour in enough water to come about halfway up the mixture.
Simmer on low for 8 minutes, stirring, until the sauce is dark, thick and glossy and clings to the spoon.
Cook the noodles in plenty of boiling water for the time on the package, then drain and toss with the black vinegar.
Pile the noodles in a bowl, spoon the hot sauce over and top with the cucumber, carrot, daikon and scallion greens. Toss everything together at the table.
recipes.tip: The sauce keeps for 4 days in the fridge. Make a double batch and you have a 10-minute lunch waiting.

recipes.name: Mapo tofu with beef and shiitake, with oyster-sauce gai lan and mixed rice
recipes.inspiredBy: Sichuan mapo doufu, with lean beef, mushrooms mixed in and a bowl of greens to go with it
recipes.about: Soft tofu in a spicy, savoury sauce built on doubanjiang, with a little lean beef (the traditional Sichuan way) and a lot of diced shiitake that melt into the sauce. Toasted, ground Sichuan pepper brings the numbing tingle, and gai lan with oyster sauce cools it down. It makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done, and the **tofu and gai lan carry calcium**.

ingredients.note: soft or medium-firm, calcium-set, check the label for calcium sulphate

steps: Toast the Sichuan peppercorns in a dry pan over medium heat for about a minute, until they smell citrusy, then grind them to a coarse powder. Cut the tofu into 2 cm cubes. Slide them into a pot of hot water with a good pinch of salt, steaming but not boiling, and leave them for 2 minutes, then drain gently. This seasons the tofu and firms it so it does not break apart in the sauce.
Finely dice the shiitake so it is about the size of the minced beef. Mince the garlic and ginger and slice the scallion. Stir the cornstarch with a few tablespoons of cold water until smooth.

Heat the oil in a wok or wide pan over medium-high heat. Cook the beef and shiitake together, breaking the beef up, for 4 to 5 minutes, until the beef is browned all the way through (71 °C / 160 °F) and the mushroom liquid has cooked off. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw beef.

Push the meat to one side and add the doubanjiang. Fry it for about a minute, until the oil turns red and it smells toasty and deep. This is the heart of the dish. Add the garlic and ginger for 15 seconds, then pour in enough water that the tofu will sit about half-submerged.
Slide in the tofu and gently nudge it with the back of the spoon rather than stirring, so the cubes stay whole. Simmer for 5 minutes.

Stir the cornstarch again and pour it in in three goes, nudging the pan after each, until the sauce turns glossy and clings to the tofu. Simmer 1 minute more, then sprinkle with the Sichuan pepper and the scallion.
Boil the gai lan in a pot of water for 2 minutes, until the stems are crisp-tender and bright green. Drain and toss with the oyster sauce.
Reheat the rice and barley and serve the mapo tofu over it with the gai lan on the side. Pack only the second portion of mapo tofu and rice for tomorrow's lunch, and boil fresh gai lan to go with it.
recipes.tip: Want it milder? Use half the doubanjiang and taste before you add more.

recipes.name: Pan-seared salmon with ginger scallion oil, garlic bok choy and mixed rice
recipes.inspiredBy: the Cantonese and Shanghainese habit of pouring sizzling oil over ginger and scallion, here on pan-seared salmon
recipes.about: A crisp-skinned salmon fillet with a sharp, fragrant sauce of ginger and scallion that sizzles when hot oil hits it, with black vinegar and soy stirred in. Garlicky bok choy and rice and barley complete the plate in about 25 minutes. **Salmon is rich in omega-3 fats** and vitamin D, and the vinegar cuts through the richness.
steps: Take the salmon out of the fridge 10 minutes ahead and pat it very dry. Season both sides with a pinch of the salt. Reheat the rice and barley.
Finely chop the ginger and scallion and put them in a small heatproof bowl with a tiny pinch of salt. Thinly slice the garlic.

Warm a third of the oil in a non-stick or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat. Lay the salmon in, skin side down, and press it gently for 10 seconds so the skin makes full contact. Cook without moving it for 4 minutes, until the skin is crisp and the flesh has turned opaque two thirds of the way up. Flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more, until it just flakes. Move it to a plate.
Wipe the pan, add the rest of the oil and heat it until it shimmers, about a minute. Carefully pour it over the ginger and scallion. It will sizzle and spit. Stir in the soy sauce and black vinegar.
Return the pan to the heat with the bok choy, the garlic and a splash of water. Cover and steam for 2 minutes, until the stems are just tender, then drizzle with the sesame oil.
Serve the salmon on the rice and barley with the sauce spooned over and the bok choy beside it.
recipes.tip: No bok choy? Any leafy green steamed the same way works, and the sauce is excellent on plain steamed fish, too.

recipes.name: Stir-fried chicken with snow peas, shiitake, carrot and almonds, over mixed rice
recipes.inspiredBy: Cantonese stir-fried chicken with snow peas and carrot, in a light oyster sauce, with toasted almonds as in almond chicken
recipes.about: Tender strips of chicken thigh with crunchy snow peas, sweet carrot and meaty shiitake in a light oyster sauce, tossed in a very hot wok so everything stays crisp, with toasted almonds scattered on top. It makes two portions and packs well into a lunch box. The almonds bring **vitamin E and crunch**, and the snow peas add vitamin C.
steps: Toss the chicken with the broth and half the cornstarch and leave it for 10 minutes. This light coating keeps it juicy in the hot pan.

Meanwhile, toast the almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes, until they smell nutty. Slice the carrot into thin coins, slice the shiitake, mince the ginger and garlic, and slice the scallion. Stir the oyster sauce and the rest of the cornstarch into a few tablespoons of water.

Heat a wok or wide pan over high heat until it is almost smoking. Add half the oil and the chicken, in two batches because two portions crowd a home wok. Spread it out and leave it alone for 30 seconds so it browns, then stir-fry for 2 minutes, until cooked through. Move it to a plate.

Add the rest of the oil, then the ginger, garlic, shiitake and carrot and stir-fry for 3 minutes, until the mushrooms are golden and the carrot is just tender. Add the snow peas and stir-fry for 1 minute more. Keep everything moving and the vegetables will stay crisp.
Return the chicken, stir the oyster sauce mixture again and pour it in, then toss for 30 seconds, until glossy. Finish with the scallion and the almonds.

Reheat the rice and barley and serve the chicken over it. Pack the second portion, rice and all, for tomorrow's lunch, and reheat it in a hot pan rather than the microwave so the vegetables stay crisp.
recipes.tip: Snow peas can swap for sugar snaps, and toasted cashews work in place of the almonds.

recipes.name: Sichuan-style braised mackerel and tofu in doubanjiang sauce, with garlic gai lan
recipes.inspiredBy: Sichuan doubanyu, fish braised in chili bean paste, made with mackerel and tofu
recipes.about: Mackerel pieces seared until golden, then braised in a spicy, savoury doubanjiang sauce with ginger, garlic, a touch of sugar and black vinegar, with cubes of tofu soaking up the sauce. Cold garlic gai lan on the side cools things down. **Mackerel is rich in omega-3 fats** and vitamin D, and the strong sauce suits it perfectly.

ingredients.note: fillets or steaks, cut into chunks
calcium-set, check the label for calcium sulphate

steps: Cut the mackerel into 3 cm chunks and pat them very dry. Sprinkle them with a pinch of white pepper. Cut the tofu into thick slabs. Mince the ginger and half the garlic, and slice the scallion. Reheat the rice and barley.

Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Lay in the mackerel, skin side down, and sear for 2 minutes without moving it, then turn and sear 1 minute more, until golden. Take it out and set it on a plate.

Turn the heat down to medium. Add the doubanjiang to the oil left in the pan and fry for about a minute, until the oil turns red. Add the ginger and the garlic for 15 seconds, then pour in enough water to come about halfway up where the fish will sit, along with the broth, the sugar and the black vinegar.

Bring it to a simmer and slide in the tofu. Put the fish back in, skin side up, and simmer gently for 6 minutes, spooning the sauce over the top now and then instead of stirring, so the fish stays whole.
Meanwhile, boil the gai lan for 2 minutes, until the stems are crisp-tender, then drain and rinse under cold water. Toss it with the rest of the garlic, finely minced, and the sesame oil.
Spoon the fish, tofu and plenty of sauce over the rice and barley. Sprinkle with the scallion and serve with the cold gai lan.
recipes.tip: Not a fan of mackerel? Salmon steaks are good in the same sauce.

recipes.name: Red-braised beef shank with daikon, carrots, eggs and napa cabbage
recipes.inspiredBy: Shanghainese red-braising (hong shao), the soy sauce and caramelized sugar braise used for beef and chicken
recipes.about: Beef shank simmered slowly in soy sauce, a splash of chicken broth, caramelized sugar, ginger and star anise until the meat is fork-tender and the sauce turns dark and glossy, with daikon, carrot and a braised egg soaking up all of it and napa cabbage wilted in at the end. It takes patience but very little work, and it tastes even better tomorrow. The **beef gives you iron and zinc**.
steps: Put the beef in a pot of cold water, bring it to a boil and cook for 3 minutes, until grey scum rises. Drain and rinse the beef. This gives you a clean, clear sauce. Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool them in cold water and peel.

Warm the oil in a heavy pot over medium-low heat, add the sugar and stir for 1 to 2 minutes, until it melts into an amber syrup. This is what gives red-braised dishes their colour and gloss. Add the sliced ginger and the scallion whites and stir for 30 seconds, then add the beef and stir for 2 minutes to coat it.
Pour in the broth and soy sauce, add the star anise and pour in enough water to just cover the beef. Bring to a boil, then turn the heat down low, cover and simmer for 90 minutes.
Add the daikon, carrot and peeled eggs, cover again and simmer for 25 minutes more, until the beef is fork-tender and the daikon looks translucent.

Stir in the napa cabbage and simmer for 5 minutes with the lid off. If the sauce is thin, turn the heat up for the last couple of minutes and let it bubble down until it is glossy and clings to the beef.
Reheat the rice and barley and serve the beef, vegetables and a halved egg over it with the scallion greens. Pack the second portion for tomorrow's lunch.
recipes.tip: Start it as soon as you walk in, or use a pressure cooker, where the beef is tender in 35 minutes. A double batch is no more work and freezes very well.

recipes.name: Homemade beef, shrimp and napa dumplings in whole-wheat wrappers, with black vinegar and smashed cucumber
recipes.inspiredBy: Northern Chinese jiaozi, with a hot-water whole-wheat dough and plenty of cabbage in the filling
recipes.about: Plump boiled dumplings filled with lean beef, sweet shrimp, napa cabbage, ginger and scallion, wrapped in a tender hot-water dough made with whole-wheat flour, and served with a sharp black vinegar dip and a garlicky smashed cucumber. It is the weekend project: put on music and fold with someone. The **whole-wheat wrappers and cabbage add fibre**.
steps: Make the dough. Put the flour in a bowl and stir in just-boiled water a splash at a time (about 60% as much water as flour by weight) with chopsticks until it looks shaggy. When it is cool enough to touch, knead for 5 minutes, until smooth. Cover and rest it for 30 minutes. The hot water softens the whole-wheat bran, so the wrappers stay tender.

Make the filling. Toss the shredded napa with the salt and leave it for 10 minutes, then squeeze it very dry in a clean towel. Mix it with the beef, the finely chopped shrimp, minced ginger, finely chopped scallion, soy sauce, broth, about half the canola oil and half the sesame oil. Stir in one direction for a minute, then stir in cold water a spoonful at a time, until the lean filling is moist and sticky. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw beef and shrimp.

Roll the dough into a long rope and cut it into pieces about the size of a large grape. Flatten each piece and roll it into a thin round about 7 cm wide, a little thinner at the edge than in the middle.
Put a generous tablespoon of filling in each wrapper, fold it in half and pinch the edge shut. Set the finished dumplings on a floured tray, not touching.

Boil them in a big pot of water, in batches, stirring gently so they do not stick. When they float, add a splash of cold water, and repeat that once more. They are done about 1 minute after the second splash, about 6 minutes in all. Cut one open to check: the filling should be 71 °C (160 °F) and no longer pink.

For the dip, stir the black vinegar with a few drops of sesame oil. Smash only half the cucumber with the flat of a knife, chop it roughly and toss it with the minced garlic and a few drops of vinegar and sesame oil. Smash the rest fresh tomorrow, because it turns watery overnight.

Eat half the dumplings with the dip and the cucumber. Cool the rest for tomorrow's lunch, then pan-fry them in the rest of the canola oil with a splash of water and the lid on for 3 minutes, until crisp on the bottom and hot through.
recipes.tip: Fold double and freeze the raw dumplings on a tray, then bag them. They boil straight from frozen in 7 to 8 minutes.

recipes.name: Whole steamed sea bass with ginger, scallion and hot oil, gai lan and mixed rice
recipes.inspiredBy: the Cantonese steamed fish served at family dinners, with ginger, scallion and sizzling oil
recipes.about: A whole sea bass steamed for just 8 to 10 minutes over soft tofu until the flesh is silky, topped with fine threads of ginger and scallion and a splash of sizzling oil and soy sauce. Gai lan and rice make it a full Sunday dinner, and it is much easier than it looks. The steamed fish is a **very lean protein**, and the tofu and gai lan add calcium.

ingredients.note: one whole sea bass or branzino, about 400 g cleaned; this is the edible weight
calcium-set, check the label for calcium sulphate, cut into thick slabs

steps: Ask the fishmonger to scale and gut the fish. Pat it dry and cut two or three slashes into each side. Rub it inside and out with the salt, and a pinch of white pepper.

Cut half the ginger into slices and half the scallion into lengths. Tuck some inside the fish. Lay the rest on a heatproof plate with the tofu slabs, then set the fish on top so the fish sits off the plate and the tofu soaks up the juices.

Set up a steamer: a wok or wide pot with a rack and a lid. Bring about 4 cm of water to a rolling boil, lower in the plate, cover and steam on high for 8 to 10 minutes. The fish is done when the flesh at the thickest part is opaque and pulls easily from the bone.
While it steams, cut the rest of the ginger and the green parts of the scallion into very fine threads. Warm the soy sauce with the broth and 2 tablespoons of hot water.
Lift the plate out and pour off the cloudy liquid. Pick off the cooked ginger and scallion and discard them. Pile the fresh threads on top of the fish, with the tofu alongside.

Heat the oil in a small pot until it shimmers. Spoon a teaspoon of it into a bowl and set it aside, then pour the rest over the threads, which sizzle and release their smell. Pour most of the warm soy sauce around the fish.
Boil the gai lan for 2 minutes, drain and toss with the sliced garlic, the reserved hot oil and the rest of the soy sauce. Reheat the rice and barley and serve everything together.
recipes.tip: No steamer? Set the plate on a bowl placed upside-down in a big pot with a lid. The steaming time stays the same.

recipes.name: Mandarin and roasted peanuts
recipes.about: A juicy mandarin with a small handful of roasted peanuts, a snack you will find at any Chinese market stall. It is sweet, salty and crunchy. The **peanuts bring protein and vitamin E**, and the mandarin adds vitamin C.
steps: Peel the mandarin and eat it with the peanuts.

recipes.name: Mandarin and toasted almonds
recipes.about: A juicy mandarin with a handful of toasted almonds, sweet and crunchy together. The almonds are the **best vitamin E source** in the week's snacks, and the mandarin adds vitamin C.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes, until they smell nutty. Peel the mandarin and eat it with the almonds.

recipes.name: Roasted sweet potato (kao hongshu)
recipes.about: A whole sweet potato roasted until the skin crackles and the inside turns jammy and caramelized, the way it is sold from street carts all over northern China in winter. Nothing is added. It is full of **vitamin A and fibre**.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Pierce the sweet potato a few times with a fork, set it on a tray and roast for 45 to 50 minutes, until it feels very soft and some syrup oozes out.
Let it cool for a few minutes and eat it with the skin on.
recipes.tip: Roast a whole tray on Sunday and rewarm one in a toaster oven. They keep for 4 days in the fridge.

recipes.name: Warm walnut soy milk
recipes.about: Warm, plain soy milk blended with toasted walnuts until it is creamy and nutty, a cousin of the walnut drinks sold across China. It is comforting and filling without being sweet. The soy milk brings **calcium and protein**, and the walnuts add plant omega-3.
steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes, until they smell nutty.
Warm the soy milk until steaming, then blend it with the walnuts for 30 seconds, until smooth. Drink it warm.

recipes.name: Warm almond soy milk
recipes.about: Warm, plain soy milk blended with toasted almonds until it is creamy and fragrant, in the spirit of the almond drinks sold across southern China. It is comforting and not too sweet. The soy milk brings **calcium and protein**, and the almonds add vitamin E.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes, until they smell nutty.
Warm the soy milk until steaming, then blend it with the almonds for 30 seconds, until smooth. Drink it warm.
recipes.inspiredBy: Chinese almond soy drinks (xingren dou jiang)

recipes.name: Mandarins
recipes.about: Two juicy mandarins, the fruit that sits in a bowl in every Chinese home from autumn on. They are sweet, easy and refreshing. The mandarins bring **vitamin C and fibre** for almost no effort.
steps: Peel the mandarins and eat them in segments.

recipes.name: Asian pear with toasted almonds
recipes.about: Crisp, juicy Asian pear slices with toasted almonds. Pear is a very Chinese fruit to snack on, and it is cool and refreshing. The **almonds bring vitamin E and magnesium**.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 2 minutes, until they smell nutty.
Slice the pear and eat it with the almonds.

recipes.name: Asian pear with walnuts
recipes.about: Crisp Asian pear with a handful of walnuts, sweet and crunchy together. It is quick, filling and travels well. The **walnuts add plant omega-3 fats**, and the pear adds fibre.
steps: Slice the pear and eat it with the walnuts. Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes first if you like.

recipes.name: Cold tofu with scallion, soy and sesame oil
recipes.about: A block of cool, soft tofu with finely sliced scallion, a few drops of soy sauce and sesame oil, one of the simplest and most loved cold dishes (xiaocong ban doufu) in China. It is savoury and fresh. The tofu brings **calcium and plant protein**.

ingredients.note: calcium-set, check the label for calcium sulphate

steps: Drain the tofu and set it on a plate. Slice it into big squares, or leave it whole and break it up with a spoon.
Scatter on the finely sliced scallion and the sesame seeds, then dribble over the soy sauce and the sesame oil.
recipes.inspiredBy: xiaocong ban doufu, Chinese tofu tossed with scallion

recipes.name: Warm edamame with Sichuan pepper salt
recipes.about: Warm, steamy edamame tossed with a pinch of salt and toasted, ground Sichuan pepper for a numbing tingle, in the spirit of Sichuan snack tables. It is a fun thing to nibble on. Edamame brings **plant protein, folate and fibre**.
steps: Boil the edamame in water for 4 minutes, until tender, then drain.
Toast the Sichuan peppercorns in a dry pan for 1 minute, until fragrant, then grind them. Toss the edamame with the salt and the pepper and eat while warm.

recipes.name: Smashed cucumber with garlic, black vinegar and peanuts
recipes.about: Cucumber smashed with the flat of a knife so it soaks up a sharp, garlicky dressing, with crushed roasted peanuts on top. It is cool, tangy and crunchy, and takes five minutes. The **peanuts bring vitamin E and protein** to a very light snack.
steps: Smash the cucumber with the flat of a knife until it splits, then chop it into bite-size pieces.
Toss it with the minced garlic, black vinegar, sesame oil and salt. Top with the crushed peanuts.
recipes.inspiredBy: Sichuan and northern Chinese smashed cucumber (pai huanggua)
